posts.text:
Back in July I took Otani san and Yamazaki san down to Hambantota to visit the Lanka Salt saltern. We walked the pans at sunset, then spent the evening inside a few small processing centres nearby, tasting samples and talking to the people who run the machines.
 
We went with two questions.
 
Our Japanese partners were asking whether Sri Lankan salt, and what comes out alongside it, could feed beauty and personal care manufacturing in Japan. Gypsum settles in the concentrating ponds. Magnesium stays in the bittern left after harvest, the same raw material Japan knows as nigari. The pink colour in the crystalliser ponds comes from Dunaliella salina, a microalga whose carotenoid extracts already go into skincare. Most of it never leaves Hambantota as anything more than raw salt.
 
My own question was what a modern salt processing line would look like if we built it today, with sensors, embedded control and AI watching the evaporation, crystallisation and separation steps instead of relying on experience alone. The engineering is not the hard part. The hard part is that nobody has had the resources to try.
 
That gap is where SoftSora can be useful. We bring the technical side, AI, embedded systems and automation, and we bring the Japanese relationships that turn a pilot into a buyer. Ideas like this usually stall somewhere between the field and the factory. That is the part we are working on.

Was glad to join Path to Internship 2026 at SLIIT as a panelist. It's my own university, so it meant a bit more to be back.
 
My main point to the students was simple. Don't just be a consumer of AI, learn to evaluate it. Question what it gives you, judge the output, and know when it's wrong. That's where the real value is now. And alongside that, the basics still matter more than ever. Attitude, critical thinking, and taking ownership of your work.
 
Well done to the IEEE Student Branch and IEEE IAS teams at SLIIT for putting this together. Thanks for having me, and good luck to everyone who took part.
 
#SoftSora #SLIIT #PathToInternship #PTI2026 #IEEE #SriLanka

Last month we had the privilege of hosting Tomoaki Otani san, CEO of Frontieer Japan LLC, at our Colombo office for three weeks.

For anyone who knows the SoftSora story, Otani san is not just a business partner. He is one of the people who helped lay the foundation this company stands on today. Long before we had the team and the client base we have now across Japan and Europe, he believed in what a Sri Lankan team could deliver to Japanese enterprise standards.

Those three weeks were anything but a formal visit. Working sessions with our engineers. Deep dives into live projects. Honest feedback on quality, process and how Japanese clients think. Our team asked questions, challenged ideas and learned directly from someone who has spent his career building trust across two very different business cultures.

Seeing our younger engineers sit with him, some of them presenting to a Japanese client stakeholder for the first time, was the highlight of the month for all of us.

Otani san, thank you for the time, the honesty and the belief. The plaque our team put together says it better than words here can.

Here is to the next chapter of the Frontieer Japan and SoftSora partnership.

いつもありがとうございます。

#SoftSora #FrontieerJapan #SriLanka #Japan #Partnership #GlobalTeams

posts.text:
Every founder has a handful of people who believed early, when believing was not the obvious choice. Tomoaki Otani san is one of mine.

He took a chance on us when SoftSora was still an idea with more ambition than proof. Three weeks with our team in Colombo last month, and he was still doing what he has always done, teaching, questioning, pushing us to be better. Watching him share the same patience with our young engineers that he once showed me was something I will not forget.

Frontieer Japan and SoftSora have built a lot together. I think the best part is still ahead.

Thank you, always.

After months of silent work, I'm excited to finally share the new project we're bringing forward in DWorld VR together with SoftSora Nilan Meegoda Mohammed Rishard Riccardo Romoli: Touli 🎁 
Touli will become the new mobile citizen and enterprise engagement layer of the DWorld ecosystem to generate real social impact. It's not a coincidence that we'll start this project from my city of birth, Genoa in Italy. Touli is an authentic Genoese word that means something close to “there it is,” “look at that,” or “there you go.” 
Hence, deeply rooted in the Genoese spirit of the city where I'm coming from, Touli carries the energy of spontaneous discovery: the feeling of recognising that something meaningful is happening. 
And that's what we are here for. To create real impact that can be seen and can influence others to contribute to their society spontaneously.

There it is! Touli is soon to be launched and we are so excited to share all our next milestones ahead at DWorld VR 💫

posts.text: It has been a genuine privilege to partner with Manila Di Giovanni  and the DWorld VR team on Touli. We at SoftSora are proud to contribute to a platform designed to create meaningful and measurable social impact, and we look forward to the milestones ahead as Touli launches in Genoa and beyond.

🍵 Almost a year ago, I was sitting at a small table in Tokyo with our partners in Japan, drinking matcha.

If you have ever watched matcha being made, you know it is not fast. The leaves are ground slowly into a fine powder, no shortcuts, just patience. What comes out is smooth, clean, and worth the wait.

That is exactly how building SoftSora in Japan has felt.

We did not arrive overnight. For three years we have delivered AI and software engineering to Japanese enterprises, and that market teaches you one thing above all else, shortcuts get caught. The documentation, the bilingual coordination, the obsession with quality, the trust you earn one project at a time,  that was the grind. And like good matcha, the result was worth every bit of it.

I have a deep respect for Japanese culture and the discipline behind it. That standard is now part of who we are.

This September, we take the next step. SoftSora will be exhibiting at the Overseas Business EXPO 2026 Tokyo (海外ビジネスEXPO) on 17–18 September at Hamamatsucho, together with our Japanese partner. This year's theme is "Overseas Business in the AI Era" exactly the conversation we are here to have.

What we bring is simple, a team of highly skilled Sri Lankan engineers who pair real AI capability with the delivery standards Japan trained us to meet.

If you are exploring AI, automation, or a cross border delivery partner you can actually trust, come find us. The tea is ready, we would love for you to visit our booth. 🇯🇵🇱🇰

Spent the first two days at the Sri Lankan-German Business Forum 2026 in Colombo, organised by AHK Sri Lanka under the theme "Building Trusted Partnerships."

Day one was the Kick-Off and Start Up Night at TRACE Expert City, with pitches from early stage founders across sectors, including one building AI tools for drug discovery. Day two moved to the main conference at ITC Ratnadipa, with panels on ports as regional gateways, EU expectations on digitalization and sustainability, and how German and Sri Lankan companies build trust that outlasts a single project cycle.

For us at SoftSora this is not theory. We have spent years earning that trust with Japanese enterprises, and we are now carrying the same discipline into the German and European market. The opportunity is real, but it belongs to the companies willing to show up, listen, and deliver consistently.

Good to have met Dr. Felix Neumann, German Ambassador to Sri Lanka and the Maldives, along with many others working to make this corridor stronger.
